That reach gives the group meaningful room to adjust prices as CPI and PPI remain elevated. Investors watching its P/E discount and high dividend may focus less on that headline yield and more on what happens if one unseen pressure on cash generation persists.

The company gives you direct exposure to the inflation resilient 7-Eleven ecosystem. Essential groceries, convenience services, and logistics infrastructure combine with steady foot traffic and pricing power. Recent CPI and PPI data suggest that small shifts in how far customers absorb higher shelf and energy costs could matter a lot if one unseen pressure on spending habits changes.

full_texts.title: Tensions persist a year after remarks on regional conflict
full_texts.text:
Nov. 8 (Asia Today) -- A year has passed since the head of government said the country could exercise its right to collective self-defense in the event of an armed conflict in the Strait, but diplomatic tensions with a neighbouring country show little sign of easing.
[the country] continues to demand that the head of government retract her parliamentary remarks, while the capital has maintained its position and sought opportunities for dialogue.
The country has postponed the possible expulsion of a consul general from the neighbouring country to prevent further diplomatic escalation. At the same time, companies and government agencies in the country are diversifying their rare earth supplies in response to export restrictions from the neighbouring country.
The dispute also has implications for a major trading partner, given the importance of stability in the Strait and the availability of critical minerals used in electric vehicles and other advanced manufacturing industries.
Diplomatic dispute enters second year
The controversy began on Nov. 7, 2025, when the head of government told a budget committee of the country's House of Representatives that a naval blockade of the country involving military force could constitute a situation threatening the country's survival.
Such a designation is one of the legal conditions under which the country can exercise its right to collective self-defense.
Previous governments had generally avoided specifying circumstances in which the country might use military force in response to a contingency involving the neighbouring country.
The neighbouring country interpreted the head of government's statement as suggesting that the country could intervene militarily in the issue.
The head of government subsequently said any decision would depend on the circumstances of a particular situation but refused to withdraw her remarks.
According to a local newspaper, the consul general from the neighbouring country posted threatening remarks on social media targeting the head of government, including language referring to beheading her.
The government considered expelling him.
When the country's Foreign Ministry communicated that possibility to [the country], officials from the neighbouring country responded that they would expel two consuls general from the country if the capital expelled one diplomat from the neighbouring country.
The head of government postponed the expulsion over concerns that reciprocal diplomatic expulsions would further damage relations.
A year later, prospects for a summit between the two countries remain uncertain.
The head of government said Friday that the country would continue pursuing dialogue with the neighbouring country, but [the country] reiterated its demand that she retract her remarks.
A local news agency reported that a meeting between the head of government and the president of the neighbouring country on the sidelines of this month's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit appeared increasingly unlikely.
The country diversifies rare earth supplies
A local newspaper reported that companies and government agencies in the country have been diversifying procurement sources in response to restrictions on rare earth and rare metal exports from the neighbouring country.
The country's Economy, Trade and Industry Minister described the neighbouring country's measures Friday as economic coercion.
He said the country would pursue alternative materials, expand recycling and diversify its supply sources.
The organization for metals and energy security is also revising its programs to support rare earth mine development and secure interests in refining operations.
The tourism industry in the country, meanwhile, is exploring ways to attract more visitors from other countries to offset a decline in tourists from the neighbouring country.
The neighbouring country's rare earth restrictions also pose risks for manufacturers in a major trading partner.
Permanent magnets made from rare earth elements such as neodymium are critical components in electric vehicle motors and industrial robots.
Even when companies diversify the countries supplying raw materials, vulnerabilities remain if the separation, refining and magnet manufacturing stages are concentrated in a particular country.
The major trading partner's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources announced a comprehensive rare earth supply chain strategy in February.
In July, the ministry consulted with the anti-corruption authority on financial support for overseas resource development, domestic processing capacity and recycling projects to recover materials used in permanent magnets from discarded products.
Stability in the Strait also affects the major trading partner
The major trading partner's official position emphasizes the importance of peace and stability in the Strait.
A joint fact sheet released following a summit between the major trading partner and a major power in November 2025 said both countries stressed the importance of peace and stability in the Strait and the peaceful resolution of [the country] differences.
The head of government's remarks a year ago concerned the conditions under which the country might exercise collective self-defense in a contingency involving the neighbouring country.
The major trading partner's document, by contrast, established diplomatic principles intended to prevent conflict.
The country's experience over the past year illustrates how prolonged diplomatic tensions over the issue can have implications for the major trading partner.
For the major trading partner, peace and stability in the Strait are closely linked to energy security, economic security and the stability of critical industrial supply chains.

full_texts.title: US cites pressure in PNG closure of [the country] site
full_texts.text:
The US government has expressed concern over the closure of the representative office in a neighbouring country under pressure from that country's government, saying that the incident is another example of intimidation by a major power.
"We are deeply concerned by reports that the government of the neighbouring country has unilaterally ordered the closure of the Economic Office in its capital," an unnamed US Department of State spokesman said on Saturday.
"The country is a reliable, like-minded and democratic partner, and its relationships around the world provide significant benefits to the citizens of those countries, including the neighbouring country," the spokesman said.
Photo: Reuters
"This is yet another example of the major power's intimidation campaign against the country and its supporters around the world, which undermines the sovereign decisions of countries choosing to partner with the country and threatens international peace and prosperity," the spokesman added.
The US Department of State made the remarks in response to a request for comment on the country's decision on Friday to close its representative office in the neighbouring country, which was established in 1990 despite the absence of official diplomatic ties.
The decision came after the neighbouring country renewed its unilateral demands that personnel of the Economic Office in its capital leave the country and that the office be shut down, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) said.
"In consideration of national dignity, diplomatic autonomy and overall national interests, and following a comprehensive assessment, the government has made the decision to close the office, withdraw all stationed personnel, and conduct a full review and adjustment of bilateral ties," the ministry said in a statement issued on Friday.
The dispute began after the neighbouring country's Minister of Foreign Affairs announced on July 16 that his government had ordered the immediate closure of the country's representative office in the country, citing adherence to the "one [another country]" policy.
The country promptly lodged a formal protest with the neighbouring country, but maintained that its representative office remained operational despite the unilateral announcement.
The country also suspended spot purchases of liquefied natural gas from the neighbouring country in July in response to that country's plans to close the country's representative office.
The major power has long used political coercion, economic incentives and diplomatic pressure to force other countries to accept its political claims, while seeking to limit the country's international presence, MOFA said.
The neighbouring government's decision is another example of the major power using political and economic leverage to interfere in other countries' diplomatic decisions, undermining international trust and fairness, it said, urging the international community to recognize the major power's efforts to isolate the country on the global stage.
Additional reporting by Fang Wei-li
RESTRICTING THE COUNTRY: The major power is using coercion and economic incentives to force other countries to accept its claims on the country, the MOFA said. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) said yesterday it would close its representative office in the neighbouring country and stop buying liquefied natural gas (LNG) from that country, citing pressure from the major power. The neighbouring country's minister of foreign affairs in July said the government had decided to close the country's representative office in the country immediately, winning praise from the major power, although the office had remained open in the interim. The country has decided to shut the office and withdraw all personnel on the basis of national dignity, diplomatic autonomy and the country's overall interests, the MOFA said, adding that the government will reassess and adjust.

The country and a major power might sign a wide-ranging trade agreement by the end of this year, which could help break a deadlock in the country's trade diplomacy if completed, a regional news outlet reported yesterday. The major power is negotiating with the administration of the head of government to reach a comprehensive economic agreement modeled after the Enhanced Trade Partnership Arrangement finalized by another country and the country in 2023, it said, citing two sources familiar with the matter. "The Enhanced Trade Partnership between the other country and the country sets a precedent for the major power to follow," one of the sources told the media outlet. The framework leaves room for future agreements.

A national from a major power, who was at an international airport after arriving on a connecting flight from another country on Monday and sought asylum in the country, was deported to that country early yesterday, the National Immigration Agency (NIA) said. In a video circulating on social media, the individual identified himself as a former host at a major state broadcaster and said he was seeking temporary humanitarian protection in the country. He said he was sentenced to six years in prison after he was recorded and reported to authorities in 2019 for criticizing "a ruler who loses his country." After his release, he was forced to go.

PLUMMETING: The stock index plunged 3,737.67 points in early session yesterday, the largest intraday drop in history, and closed down 1,873.08 points due to AI data center concerns. The government yesterday authorized the activation of its local currency 500 billion (US$15.26 billion) National Stabilization Fund (NSF) to support local shares, as the stock market experienced significant fluctuations while uncertainties in the international political and economic situation continue. The NSF’s steering committee may use the fund to intervene in the market to prop up local shares, the Ministry of Finance said in a statement. Once the fund is activated next week, it would be the 10th time the NSF has intervened in the market. Separately, the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) yesterday announced temporary curbs on short selling shares and other measures to help.
